newsitem.title: USA: SEC ups limit for investment companies on stock buys.
newsitem.headline: SEC ups limit for investment companies on stock buys.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday adopted rules allowing investment companies to purchase more shares from the securities offerings their affiliates underwrite.
The agency first imposed limits 57 years ago as a way to protect mutual fund shareholders by preventing affiliated underwriters from dumping their unmarketable securities into mutual funds.
The SEC hasn't made any changes to its restrictions in almost 20 years even though total mutal fund assets have grown to an excess of some $4 trillion.

"Much has changed since then," said SEC Chairman Arthur, Levitt, adding that the new rules "reflect the necessities and opportunities of today's complex and global securities markets, while continuing to protect investors."
SEC officials, said the changes were needed because the financial services industry has changed so dramatically and would do so even more with the passage of pending reforms in Congress.

Under the new rules, investment companies would be allowed to purchase up to 25 percent of such offerings, a substantial increase from the previous 4 percent limit. Last year, the SEC first proposed raising the limit to 10 percent.

Mutual fund industry representatives urged the agency to do away with the percentage limit altogether, claiming adequate safeguards were in place to curb dumping. But agency officials said they were unconvinced at this time that there is a case for moving in that direction.
Levitt cautioned that the latest limit increase "does not reflect a judgment by the commission that a certain amount of dumping is acceptable.

"Protecting investors from this type of overreaching by fund affiliates is, and should always remain, a core principle," Levitt said. "I assure you that the commission will deal harshly with any company that acts contrary to the interests of fund shareholders."

Previously, the rules did not apply to foreign offerings, but now investment companies could buy up to 25 percent of foreign securities offerings from their affiliated underwriters if there is ample disclosure and a single offering price.
